1\. Legacy subclasses fail dispatch 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness 
Removing the subclass adapters makes Flask 3.1-style overrides such as dispatch_request(self)
receive an unexpected AppContext, causing request dispatch or teardown to fail with TypeError.
The deleted warning explicitly promised support until Flask 4.0, while this branch is the unreleased
3.2 release.
Agent Prompt ``` ## Issue description Removing `Flask.__init_subclass__` and its argument adapters breaks subclasses overriding lifecycle methods with their Flask 3.1 signatures. Internal dispatch now passes an `AppContext` unconditionally, so these overrides raise `TypeError` despite the compatibility period previously extending through Flask 3.x. ## Issue Context Restore compatibility without globally mutating methods on `Flask`, or retain the released method signatures and obtain the active context internally. Add regression tests covering old-signature dispatch, error handling, response processing, and teardown overrides, including overrides that call `super()`. ## Fix Focus Areas - src/flask/app.py[79-79] - src/flask/app.py[882-935] - src/flask/app.py[1282-1370] ``` ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools
